Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the NovaRetail Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during the presentation portion of the call. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to NovaRetail's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Taylor Kim, COO; Riley Patel, CMO; Morgan Chen, CTO; and Casey Lopez, CDO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, CEO of NovaRetail.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q3 performance, driven by improved advertising and marketing spend efficiency with solid ROAS, positive shifts in seller behavior following our marketplace fee updates, and rising order frequency reflecting evolving customer purchasing habits. We saw significant growth in key metrics like GMV up 15% year-over-year to $18.2 billion and active customers expanding by 12% to 120 million.

Our focus remains on gross margin expansion through product mix optimization and supply chain efficiencies. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our holiday season preparations, which position us well for peak demand. 

We are investing heavily in customer acquisition strategies that enhance CAC efficiency and ROI from our marketing efforts.

We are focused on improving seller services and value-added offerings to boost adoption and revenue diversification.

We are expanding our presence in high-growth regions like APAC while navigating fee structure impacts.

Finally, we are committed to leveraging data and technology to sustain these trends into Q4 and beyond.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. Our Q3 revenue was $12.3 billion, an increase of 18% year-over-year. Gross margin was 28.4%, driven by product mix shifts toward higher-margin private labels, supply chain efficiencies from nearshoring, and disciplined vendor take rates—up 110 basis points year-over-year and marking our sixth straight quarter of expansion. This outperforms the e-commerce peer average of around 25%, reflecting trends like private label penetration at 32% of GMV delivering 42% margins versus 24% for third-party sellers, alongside inbound freight costs dropping to 5.1% of COGS through Mexico and Vietnam sourcing, and last-mile costs at 12.3% of revenue via our nexHub network.

Operating expenses were $3.2 billion, representing 26% of revenue. On advertising and marketing spend efficiency, particularly Return on Ad Spend or ROAS—a cornerstone metric calculated as ad-attributed revenue divided by total ad spend—our blended ROAS across all channels came in at 5.2x, a sequential improvement from 4.8x in Q2 and up 16% year-over-year from 4.5x. This drove $1.2 billion in ad-attributed revenue on $230 million of total ad spend, about 12% of our $9.8 billion GMV wait no, scaling to our full GMV, representing strong performance outperforming mid-tier peers like Wayfair or ASOS at around 4x and closing in on Amazon's 6x.

By channel, Google Ads at 35% of spend delivered 7.1x ROAS with Performance Max and Shopping tabs post-Google's algorithm update, a 22% incrementality uplift from ML-powered feeds prioritizing high-margin private-label kitchenware at 45% gross margins. Meta at 28% of spend hit 4.2x, countering fashion saturation with Advantage+ Shopping Campaigns improving creative efficiency by 30% via AI assets. Amazon DSP and Sponsored Products at 20% achieved 6.3x with ACoS at 16% versus marketplace 22%, capturing high-intent in beauty and home goods.

Regionally, North America at 55% GMV saw 5.5x ROAS amid back-to-school and resilient U.S. consumers despite 3.2% inflation. EMEA at 4.7x faced GDPR and Digital Markets Act pressures, mitigated by server-side tagging. APAC shone at 5.8x, led by TikTok Shop in Southeast Asia at 8x for fast-fashion and Tmall at 6.5x for Singles' Day prep.

Trends show 12% quarter-over-quarter ROAS gains from data-driven multi-touch attribution in Google Analytics 4 and our CDP, dropping CAC 8% to $42 with LTV/CAC at 3.8x. Initiatives like NovaDSP with reinforcement learning cut bid waste 18%, first-party data from 45 million loyalty users, Privacy Sandbox pilots at 5.5x, and 65% incremental ad lift. We're shifting 15% budget to performance channels and retail media like our Nova Media Network monetizing 150 million visitors, with Criteo partnerships at 9x for abandoned carts, prioritizing premium beauty at 6.8x.

For Q4, we guide blended ROAS of 5.3x to 5.5x, supporting 18-20% ad spend growth and 14% Adjusted EBITDA margins.

Customer acquisition cost efficiency ties closely here—our blended CAC was $42.30, down 14% year-over-year from $49.20 and 5% sequentially, with 22% more new customers at 1.2 million on 18% higher $50.7 million spend. ROAS at 4.8x delivered $243 million revenue, LTV/CAC 3.8x with six-month payback at 1.5x and projected $165 LTV on 28% repeats and $85 AOV, below fashion median $56 and beating Wayfair's 4.1x.

Paid social at 45% spend gave 5.9x ROAS and $28 CAC via Meta and TikTok AI creatives with 32% CTR uplift from UGC micro-influencers. Google at 5.2x and $51 CAC shifted to YouTube Shorts. Affiliates at 6.7x and $24 CAC via Rakuten. Owned channels near-zero CAC at 12x. Server-side tracking hit 92% match rates. Tech like NovaPredict cut CAC 28% predicting intent, cookieless UID2, RCTs confirming 62% incrementality, app synergies at $18 CAC.

North America $58 CAC at 4.3x despite Temu blitz; Europe $38 at 5.6x; APAC $26 at 7.2x on TikTok; Q3 guide $40 CAC and 5.0x ROAS.

On order frequency, a leading indicator where 70% revenue from repeats, we hit 4.7 orders per active customer, up 12% year-over-year from 4.2 and 18% above pre-pandemic 4.0, beating industry 3.8 and Walmart's 4.3. Cohorts up 15%, grocery at 28% orders. Repeats at 6.2 orders, health & wellness 2.1, fashion 3.9 with style bundles up 11% add-ons. North America 5.1 on 42 million ShopSphere Prime at 2.3x non-subs; Europe 4.3; APAC 4.0 surging 20% on TikTok and Alibaba.

Tech like multimodal LLM on 1.2 trillion signals upped conversions 17%, ShopSphere Loop subscriptions at 9.2 orders for 22% recurring. BOPIS up 25% at 18% frequency. Q4 to 4.9 on holidays.

Regarding marketplace fee structure updates in late Q2—referral fees up 1.5-2 points in electronics to 16.5%, apparel 14.8%, beauty 17.2%, with grocery preserved; RCF storage up 8% offset by inbound cuts and peak waivers; tiered rebates for $50M+ at 5% reduction; ad CPC up 10% with 20% ROAS guarantees. Benchmarked to Amazon, Shopify hikes.

Seller metrics: active sellers 2.52M up 3%, small down 8% to 65% with 15% churn to Walmart/Temu; mid-tier up 11%; enterprise up 155% to 11%; avg GMV $88K up 22%; churn 13%. Polarization: small reduced SKUs 35%, enterprise GMV share to 58% with 41% multi-channel. Private labels up 47%, pricing up 9%, dynamic pricing 68%. Ad spend up 35% QoQ. North America churn 9%; Europe 18% offset; APAC +45% adds.

Seller Central 2.0 with Fee Forecaster, Inventory Optimizer cutting costs 11%, multi-channel dashboard. Take rate to 14.8%, Q4 churn to 11%, GMV 11-13%.

Seller services revenue $4.2B up 32%, 28% of net revenue. Adoption 68% overall, 85% mid/enterprise. Ads $1.8B up 45%, ARPU $285; NexFulfilled 41% at $1.1B; NexPay TPV $120B at $650M; analytics $650M. Flywheel: 2.5x GMV growth. North America 72%; Europe 38%; APAC 55%. 52% margins expanded overall by 210 bps to 48.5%. Seller OS 2.0 boosts cross-sell. FY24 30-35% growth to 75% adoption.

Our net income for the quarter was $850 million, or $1.25 per share. We ended the quarter with $4.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance of revenue $48-50 billion, gross margin 28.5-29%, and Adjusted EBITDA $5.8-6.2 billion.

On holiday prep, Q4 GMV $2.8B up 18%, 38% of year. Electronics $700M +28% AOV $450; apparel $620M +14%; home $500M +20%; beauty +16%. North America $1.54B +20%; Europe $700M +15%; APAC $420M +12%. Inventory $950M up 22% at 8.2x turns, safety +15%, 2.5M SKUs. WavePredict 96% accuracy, RFID WMS 0.2% errors, eco 60%. Risks hedged.

Now I'll turn it over to Taylor Kim to discuss operations.

Taylor Kim:
Thanks, Jordan. Operationally, we focused on supply chain nearshoring and micro-fulfillment expansion, alongside AI-driven inventory optimization. Our shipping times improved by 25% to under 1.8 days average. Fulfillment costs were down 15% to $2.10 per unit. We are implementing edge computing for real-time routing in our 40 fulfillment centers.

Now I'll turn it over to Riley Patel.

Riley Patel:
Thanks, Taylor. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from Advantage+ campaigns on Meta and Performance Max on Google, alongside TikTok Shop integrations. Customer acquisition costs were $42, with solid LTV payback. Our brand awareness increased by 18% per YouGov tracking. We are focusing on first-party data personalization and retail media networks.

Now I'll turn it over to Morgan Chen.

Morgan Chen:
Thanks, Riley. On the technology front, we've been focused on cookieless attribution via server-side tagging and multimodal LLMs for recommendations. Our website uptime was 99.98%. Mobile app usage increased by 28%. We're investing in NovaDSP for real-time bidding and Privacy Sandbox integration.

Now I'll turn it over to Casey Lopez.

Casey Lopez:
Thanks, Morgan. Data science is a key focus for us. We've seen a 17% improvement in conversion rates because of our next-gen recommendation engine analyzing trillions of signals. We are also focusing on GDPR-compliant clean rooms and incrementality testing via geo-holdouts.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
[Operator instructions for Q&A session]. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Jordan, can you expand on the ROAS drivers by channel and how you're thinking about Q4 ad auction dynamics?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, John. As I detailed, Google led at 7.1x with PMax and dynamic feeds prioritizing high-margin SKUs, Meta at 4.2x rebounding via Advantage+, Amazon at 6.3x on DSP. For Q4, stable auctions support 5.3-5.5x, with reallocation to closed-loop like Nova Media Network and TikTok, assuming no policy shifts.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen:
Great, thanks. On the fee structure updates, how has seller churn trended post-launch, and any APAC specifics?

Jordan Lee:
Emily, post-update churn stabilized at 13%, with small sellers at 15% exiting to lower-fee platforms like Temu, but enterprise adds up 155%. In APAC, +45% seller growth via UPI and RCF, winning back 60% volume despite competition, with India/SEA leading.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with JPMorgan.

Mike Rodriguez:
Thanks. Taylor, on operations, how are inventory turns holding for holidays, and any supply chain risks?

Taylor Kim:
Mike, turns at 8.2x exceeding targets, with safety stock up 15% via Monte Carlo sims. Risks like port strikes mitigated by 40% air freight and dual-sourcing, nearshoring 15% volume to Mexico.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Barclays.

Lisa Wong:
Riley, on CAC, how sustainable is the APAC efficiency, and plans for new channels?

Riley Patel:
Lisa, APAC CAC at $26 down 25% YoY on TikTok 7.2x and Shopee, with vernacular UGC. Shifting 20% to Reddit/CTV for incrementality, targeting 4.5x LTV/CAC by FY25.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Citi.

David Kim:
Thanks. Morgan, details on the LLM recs engine and mobile uplift?

Morgan Chen:
David, multimodal LLM processes 1.2 trillion signals for "next best action," upping frequency and conversions 17%, fueling 28% app usage via Firebase pushes at low CAC.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Anna Patel with UBS.

Anna Patel:
Casey, on order frequency cohorts and data privacy initiatives?

Casey Lopez:
Anna, 2023 cohorts +15% vs 2022, with Loop subs at 9.2 orders. Privacy via clean rooms and 85% consent on first-party, sustaining habits amid regs.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
